title.heading: ADDITIONS TO THE NATIONAL WILDERNESS PRESERVATION SYSTEM

paragraph.heading: Definitions.—
paragraph.chapeau: In this subsection:

subparagraph.heading: County.—
subparagraph.content: The term “County” means Hood River County, Oregon.

subparagraph.heading: Exchange map.—
subparagraph.content: The term “exchange map” means the map entitled “Cooper Spur/Government Camp Land Exchange”, dated June 2006.

subparagraph.heading: Federal land.—
subparagraph.content: The term “Federal land” means the approximately 107 acres of National Forest System land in the Mount Hood National Forest in Government Camp, Clackamas County, Oregon, identified as “USFS Land to be Conveyed” on the exchange map.

subparagraph.heading: Mt. hood meadows.—
subparagraph.content: The term “Mt. Hood Meadows” means the Mt. Hood Meadows Oregon, Limited Partnership.

subparagraph.heading: Non-federal land.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “non-Federal land” means—

clause.content: the parcel of approximately 770 acres of private land at Cooper Spur identified as “Land to be acquired by USFS” on the exchange map; and
any buildings, improvements, furniture, fixtures, and equipment at the Inn at Cooper Spur and the Cooper Spur Ski Area covered by an appraisal described in paragraph (2)(D).

subparagraph.heading: Conveyance of land.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to the provisions of this subsection, if Mt. Hood Meadows offers to convey to the United States all right, title, and interest of Mt. Hood Meadows in and to the non-Federal land, the Secretary shall convey to Mt. Hood Meadows all right, title, and interest of the United States in and to the Federal land (other than any easements reserved under subparagraph (G)), subject to valid existing rights.

subparagraph.heading: Compliance with existing law.—
subparagraph.content: Except as otherwise provided in this subsection, the Secretary shall carry out the land exchange under this subsection in accordance with section 206 of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1716).

clause.heading: Title.—
clause.content: As a condition of the land exchange under this subsection, title to the non-Federal land to be acquired by the Secretary under this subsection shall be acceptable to the Secretary.

clause.heading: Terms and conditions.—
clause.content: The conveyance of the Federal land and non-Federal land shall be subject to such terms and conditions as the Secretary may require.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of the Mount Hood Cooper Spur Land Exchange Clarification Act, the Secretary and Mt. Hood Meadows shall jointly select an appraiser to conduct an appraisal of the Federal land and non-Federal land.

clause.heading: Requirements.—
clause.chapeau: Except as provided under clause (iii), an appraisal under clause (i) shall assign a separate value to each tax lot to allow for the equalization of values and be conducted in accordance with nationally recognized appraisal standards, including—

subclause.content: the Uniform Appraisal Standards for Federal Land Acquisitions; and
the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice.

subclause.heading: In general.—
subclause.content: Subject to subclause (II), after the final appraised value of the Federal land and the non-Federal land are determined and approved by the Secretary, the Secretary shall not be required to reappraise or update the final appraised value for a period of up to 3 years, beginning on the date of the approval by the Secretary of the final appraised value.

subclause.heading: Exception.—
subclause.content: Subclause (I) shall not apply if the condition of either the Federal land or the non-Federal land referred to in subclause (I) is significantly and substantially altered by fire, windstorm, or other events.

clause.heading: Public review.—
clause.content: Before completing the land exchange under this Act, the Secretary shall make available for public review the complete appraisals of the land to be exchanged.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The exact acreage and legal description of the Federal land and non-Federal land shall be determined by surveys approved by the Secretary.

clause.heading: Costs.—
clause.content: The responsibility for the costs of any surveys conducted under clause (i), and any other administrative costs of carrying out the land exchange, shall be determined by the Secretary and Mt. Hood Meadows.

subparagraph.heading: Deadline for completion of land exchange.—
subparagraph.content: It is the intent of Congress that the land exchange under this subsection shall be completed not later than 16 months after the date of enactment of this Act.

subparagraph.heading: Required conveyance conditions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Prior to the exchange of the Federal and non-Federal land—

clause.chapeau: the Secretary and Mt. Hood Meadows may mutually agree for the Secretary to reserve a conservation easement to protect the identified wetland in accordance with applicable law, subject to the requirements that—

subclause.content: the conservation easement shall be consistent with the terms of the September 30, 2015, mediation between the Secretary and Mt. Hood Meadows; and
in order to take effect, the conservation easement shall be finalized not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of the Mount Hood Cooper Spur Land Exchange Clarification Act; and

clause.chapeau: the Secretary shall reserve a 24-foot-wide nonexclusive trail easement at the existing trail locations on the Federal land that retains for the United States existing rights to construct, reconstruct, maintain, and permit nonmotorized use by the public of existing trails subject to the right of the owner of the Federal land—

subclause.content: to cross the trails with roads, utilities, and infrastructure facilities; and
to improve or relocate the trails to accommodate development of the Federal land.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Notwithstanding subparagraph (A), in addition to or in lieu of monetary compensation, a lesser area of Federal land or non-Federal land may be conveyed if necessary to equalize appraised values of the exchange properties, without limitation, consistent with the requirements of this Act and subject to the approval of the Secretary and Mt. Hood Meadows.

clause.heading: Treatment of certain compensation or conveyances as donation.—
clause.content: If, after payment of compensation or adjustment of land area subject to exchange under this Act, the amount by which the appraised value of the land and other property conveyed by Mt. Hood Meadows under subparagraph (A) exceeds the appraised value of the land conveyed by the Secretary under subparagraph (A) shall be considered a donation by Mt. Hood Meadows to the United States.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The boundary of the Mount Hood National Forest shall be adjusted to incorporate—

clause.content: any land conveyed to the United States under paragraph (2); and
the land transferred to the Forest Service by section 1204(h)(1).

subparagraph.heading: Additions to the national forest system.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall administer the land described in subparagraph (A)—

clause.chapeau: in accordance with—

subclause.content: the Act of March 1, 1911 (commonly known as the “Weeks Law”) (16 U.S.C. 480 et seq.); and
any laws (including regulations) applicable to the National Forest System; and

clause.content: subject to sections 1202(c)(3) and 1204(d), as applicable.

subparagraph.heading: Land and water conservation fund.—
subparagraph.content: For the purposes of section 7 of the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 (16 U.S.C. 460l-9), the boundaries of the Mount Hood National Forest modified by this paragraph shall be considered to be the boundaries of the Mount Hood National Forest in existence as of January 1, 1965.

subsection.heading: Conditions on Development of Federal Land.

paragraph.heading: Requirements applicable to the conveyance of federal land.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: As a condition of each of the conveyances of Federal land under this section, the Secretary shall include in the deed of conveyance a requirement that applicable construction activities and alterations shall be conducted in accordance with—

clause.content: nationally recognized building and property maintenance codes; and
nationally recognized codes for development in the wildland-urban interface and wildfire hazard mitigation.

subparagraph.heading: Applicable law.—
subparagraph.content: To the maximum extent practicable, the codes required under subparagraph (A) shall be consistent with the nationally recognized codes adopted or referenced by the State or political subdivisions of the State.

subparagraph.heading: Enforcement.—
subparagraph.content: The requirements under subparagraph (A) may be enforced by the same entities otherwise enforcing codes, ordinances, and standards.

paragraph.heading: Compliance with codes on federal land.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall ensure that applicable construction activities and alterations undertaken or permitted by the Secretary on National Forest System land in the Mount Hood National Forest are conducted in accordance with—

subparagraph.content: nationally recognized building and property maintenance codes; and
nationally recognized codes for development in the wildland-urban interface development and wildfire hazard mitigation.

paragraph.heading: Effect on enforcement by states and political subdivisions.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subsection alters or limits the power of the State or a political subdivision of the State to implement or enforce any law (including regulations), rule, or standard relating to development or fire prevention and control. * * * * * * *

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior, shall establish a Collaborative Forest Landscape Restoration Program to select and fund ecological restoration treatments for priority forest landscapes in accordance with—

paragraph.content: the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.);
the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.); and
any other applicable law.

subsection.heading: Eligibility Criteria.—
subsection.chapeau: To be eligible for nomination under subsection (c), a collaborative forest landscape restoration proposal shall—

paragraph.chapeau: be based on a landscape restoration strategy that—

subparagraph.content: is complete or substantially complete;

subparagraph.chapeau: identifies and prioritizes ecological restoration treatments for a 10-year period within a landscape that is—

clause.content: at least 50,000 acres;

comprised primarily of forested National Forest System land, but may also include land under the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Land Management, land under the jurisdiction of the Bureau of Indian Affairs, or other Federal, State, tribal, or private land;
in need of active ecosystem restoration; and
accessible by existing or proposed wood-processing infrastructure at an appropriate scale to use woody biomass and small-diameter wood removed in ecological restoration treatments;

subparagraph.content: incorporates the best available science and scientific application tools in ecological restoration strategies;

fully maintains, or contributes toward the restoration of, the structure and composition of old growth stands according to the pre-fire suppression old growth conditions characteristic of the forest type, taking into account the contribution of the stand to landscape fire adaptation and watershed health and retaining the large trees contributing to old growth structure;

subparagraph.chapeau: would carry out any forest restoration treatments that reduce hazardous fuels by—

clause.content: focusing on small diameter trees, thinning, strategic fuel breaks, and fire use to modify fire behavior, as measured by the projected reduction of uncharacteristically severe wildfire effects for the forest type (such as adverse soil impacts, tree mortality or other impacts); and
maximizing the retention of large trees, as appropriate for the forest type, to the extent that the trees promote fire-resilient stands; and
does not include the establishment of permanent roads; and
would commit funding to decommission all temporary roads constructed to carry out the strategy;

paragraph.chapeau: be developed and implemented through a collaborative process that—

subparagraph.content: includes multiple interested persons representing diverse interests; and

clause.content: is transparent and nonexclusive; or
meets the requirements for a resource advisory committee under subsections (c) through (f) of section 205 of Public Law 106-393 (16 U.S.C. 500 note);

paragraph.chapeau: describe plans to—

subparagraph.content: reduce the risk of uncharacteristic wildfire, including through the use of fire for ecological restoration and maintenance and reestablishing natural fire regimes, where appropriate;
improve fish and wildlife habitat, including for endangered, threatened, and sensitive species;
maintain or improve water quality and watershed function;
prevent, remediate, or control invasions of exotic species;
maintain, decommission, and rehabilitate roads and trails;
use woody biomass and small-diameter trees produced from projects implementing the strategy;
report annually on performance, including through performance measures from the plan entitled the “10 Year Comprehensive Strategy Implementation Plan” and dated December 2006; and
take into account any applicable community wildfire protection plan;

paragraph.chapeau: analyze any anticipated cost savings, including those resulting from—

subparagraph.content: reduced wildfire management costs; and
a decrease in the unit costs of implementing ecological restoration treatments over time;

paragraph.chapeau: estimate—

subparagraph.content: the annual Federal funding necessary to implement the proposal; and
the amount of new non-Federal investment for carrying out the proposal that would be leveraged;

paragraph.chapeau: describe the collaborative process through which the proposal was developed, including a description of—

subparagraph.content: participation by or consultation with State, local, and Tribal governments; and

any established record of successful collaborative planning and implementation of ecological restoration projects on National Forest System land and other land included in the proposal by the collaborators; and

paragraph.chapeau: benefit local economies by providing local employment or training opportunities through contracts, grants, or agreements for restoration planning, design, implementation, or monitoring with—

subparagraph.content: local private, nonprofit, or cooperative entities;
Youth Conservation Corps crews or related partnerships, with State, local, and non-profit youth groups;
existing or proposed small or micro-businesses, clusters, or incubators; or
other entities that will hire or train local people to complete such contracts, grants, or agreements; and

paragraph.content: be subject to any other requirements that the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior, determines to be necessary for the efficient and effective administration of the program.

paragraph.heading: Submission.—
paragraph.chapeau: A proposal shall be submitted to—

subparagraph.content: the appropriate Regional Forester; and

subparagraph.chapeau: if actions under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior are proposed, the appropriate—

clause.content: State Director of the Bureau of Land Management;
Regional Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs; or
other official of the Department of the Interior.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: A Regional Forester may nominate for selection by the Secretary any proposals that meet the eligibility criteria established by subsection (b).

subparagraph.heading: Concurrence.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Any proposal nominated by the Regional Forester that proposes actions under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior shall include the concurrence of the appropriate—

clause.content: State Director of the Bureau of Land Management;
Regional Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs; or
other official of the Department of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: Documentation.—
paragraph.chapeau: With respect to each proposal that is nominated under paragraph (2)—

subparagraph.chapeau: the appropriate Regional Forester shall—

clause.content: include a plan to use Federal funds allocated to the region to fund those costs of planning and carrying out ecological restoration treatments on National Forest System land, consistent with the strategy, that would not be covered by amounts transferred to the Secretary from the Fund; and

provide evidence that amounts proposed to be transferred to the Secretary from the Fund during the first 2 fiscal years following selection would be used to carry out ecological restoration treatments consistent with the strategy during the same fiscal year in which the funds are transferred to the Secretary;

subparagraph.chapeau: if actions under the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior are proposed, the nomination shall include a plan to fund such actions, consistent with the strategy, by the appropriate—

clause.content: State Director of the Bureau of Land Management;
Regional Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs; or
other official of the Department of the Interior; and

subparagraph.content: if actions on land not under the jurisdiction of the Secretary or the Secretary of the Interior are proposed, the appropriate Regional Forester shall provide evidence that the landowner intends to participate in, and provide appropriate funding to carry out, the actions.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: After consulting with the advisory panel established under subsection (e), the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior, shall, subject to paragraph (2), select the best proposals that—

subparagraph.content: have been nominated under subsection (c)(2); and
meet the eligibility criteria established by subsection (b).

paragraph.heading: Criteria.—
paragraph.chapeau: In selecting proposals under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall give special consideration to—

subparagraph.content: the strength of the proposal and strategy;
the strength of the ecological case of the proposal and the proposed ecological restoration strategies;
the strength of the collaborative process and the likelihood of successful collaboration throughout implementation;
whether the proposal is likely to achieve reductions in long-term wildfire management costs;
whether the proposal would reduce the relative costs of carrying out ecological restoration treatments as a result of the use of woody biomass and small-diameter trees; and
whether an appropriate level of non-Federal investment would be leveraged in carrying out the proposal.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may select not more than—

subparagraph.content: 10 proposals to be funded during any fiscal year;
2 proposals in any 1 region of the National Forest System to be funded during any fiscal year; and
the number of proposals that the Secretary determines are likely to receive adequate funding.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), after consulting with the advisory panel established under subsection (e), if the Secretary determines that a proposal that has been selected under paragraph (1) and is being carried out continues to meet the eligibility criteria established by subsection (b), the Secretary, on a case-by-case basis, may issue for the proposal a 1-time extension of the 10-year period requirement under paragraph (1)(B) of that subsection.

subparagraph.heading: Limitation.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The extension described in subparagraph (A)—

clause.content: shall be for the shortest period of time practicable to complete implementation of the proposal, as determined by the Secretary; and
shall not exceed 10 years.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish and maintain an advisory panel comprised of not more than 15 members to evaluate, and provide recommendations on, each proposal that has been nominated under subsection (c)(2).

paragraph.heading: Representation.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall ensure that the membership of the advisory panel is fairly balanced in terms of the points of view represented and the functions to be performed by the advisory panel.

paragraph.heading: Inclusion.—
paragraph.content: The advisory panel shall include experts in ecological restoration, fire ecology, fire management, rural economic development, strategies for ecological adaptation to climate change, fish and wildlife ecology, and woody biomass and small-diameter tree utilization.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund, to be known as the “Collaborative Forest Landscape Restoration Fund”, to be used to pay up to 50 percent of the cost of carrying out and monitoring ecological restoration treatments on National Forest System land for each proposal selected to be carried out under subsection (d).

paragraph.heading: Inclusion.—
paragraph.content: The cost of carrying out ecological restoration treatments as provided in paragraph (1) may, as the Secretary determines to be appropriate, include cancellation and termination costs required to be obligated for contracts to carry out ecological restoration treatments on National Forest System land for each proposal selected to be carried out under subsection (d).

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.content: The Fund shall consist of such amounts as are appropriated to the Fund under paragraph (6).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: On request by the Secretary, the Secretary of the Treasury shall transfer from the Fund to the Secretary such amounts as the Secretary determines are appropriate, in accordance with paragraph (1).

subparagraph.heading: Limitation.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall not expend money from the Fund on any 1 proposal—

clause.content: during a period of more than 10 fiscal years; or
in excess of $4,000,000 in any 1 fiscal year.

subparagraph.heading: Exception.—
subparagraph.content: The limitation described in subparagraph (B)(i) shall not apply to a proposal for which a 1-time extension is granted under subsection (d)(4).

paragraph.heading: Accounting and reporting system.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish an accounting and reporting system for the Fund.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Fund $80,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023, to remain available until expended.

paragraph.heading: Work plan.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after the date on which a proposal is selected to be carried out, the Secretary shall create, in collaboration with the interested persons, an implementation work plan and budget to implement the proposal that includes—

subparagraph.content: a description of the manner in which the proposal would be implemented to achieve ecological and community economic benefit, including capacity building to accomplish restoration;

subparagraph.chapeau: a business plan that addresses

clause.content: the anticipated unit treatment cost reductions over 10 years;
the anticipated costs for infrastructure needed for the proposal;
the projected sustainability of the supply of woody biomass and small-diameter trees removed in ecological restoration treatments; and
the projected local economic benefits of the proposal;

subparagraph.content: documentation of the non-Federal investment in the priority landscape, including the sources and uses of the investments; and
a plan to decommission any temporary roads established to carry out the proposal.

paragraph.heading: Project implementation.—
paragraph.chapeau: Amounts transferred to the Secretary from the Fund shall be used to carry out ecological restoration treatments that are—

subparagraph.content: consistent with the proposal and strategy; and
identified through the collaborative process described in subsection (b)(2).

paragraph.heading: Annual report.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary, in collaboration with the Secretary of the Interior and interested persons, shall prepare an annual report on the accomplishments of each selected proposal that includes—

subparagraph.content: a description of all acres (or other appropriate unit) treated and restored through projects implementing the strategy;
an evaluation of progress, including performance measures and how prior year evaluations have contributed to improved project performance;
a description of community benefits achieved, including any local economic benefits;
the results of the multiparty monitoring, evaluation, and accountability process under paragraph (4); and

subparagraph.chapeau: a summary of the costs of—

clause.content: treatments; and
relevant fire management activities.

paragraph.heading: Multiparty monitoring.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall, in collaboration with the Secretary of the Interior and interested persons, use a multiparty monitoring, evaluation, and accountability process to assess the positive or negative ecological, social, and economic effects of projects implementing a selected proposal for not less than 15 years after project implementation commences.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 5 years after the first fiscal year in which funding is made available to carry out ecological restoration projects under the program, and every 5 years thereafter, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior, shall submit a report on the program, including an assessment of whether, and to what extent, the program is fulfilling the purposes of this title, to—

paragraph.content: the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate;
the Committee on Appropriations of the Senate;
the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate;
the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives;
the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives; and
the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives.

paragraph.heading: Affected stakeholder.—
paragraph.content: The term “affected stakeholder” means an entity that significantly affects, or is significantly affected by, the quality or quantity of water in a watershed, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Disadvantaged community.—
paragraph.content: The term “disadvantaged community” means a community (including a city, town, county, or reasonably isolated and divisible segment of a larger municipality) with an annual median household income that is less than 100 percent of the statewide annual median household income for the State in which the community is located, according to the most recent decennial census.

paragraph.heading: Grant recipient.—
paragraph.content: The term “grant recipient” means a watershed group that the Secretary has selected to receive a grant under section 6002(c)(2).

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “program” means the Cooperative Watershed Management Program established by the Secretary under section 6002(a).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

paragraph.heading: Watershed group.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “watershed group” means a self-sustaining, cooperative watershed-wide group that—

subparagraph.content: is comprised of representatives of the affected stakeholders of the relevant watershed;

subparagraph.chapeau: incorporates the perspectives of a diverse array of stakeholders, including, to the maximum extent practicable—

clause.chapeau: representatives of—

subclause.content: hydroelectric production;
livestock grazing;
timber production;
land development;
recreation or tourism;
irrigated agricultural production;
the environment;
potable water purveyors and industrial water users;
private property owners within the watershed; and
disadvantaged communities;

clause.content: any Federal agency that has authority with respect to the watershed;
any State agency that has authority with respect to the watershed;
any local agency that has authority with respect to the watershed; and

clause.chapeau: any Indian tribe that—

subclause.content: owns land within the watershed; or
has land in the watershed that is held in trust;

subparagraph.content: is a grassroots, nonregulatory entity that addresses water availability and quality issues within the relevant watershed;

subparagraph.chapeau: is capable of promoting the sustainable use of the water resources of the relevant watershed and improving the functioning condition of rivers and streams through—

clause.content: water conservation;
improved water quality;
ecological resiliency; and
the reduction of water conflicts; and

subparagraph.content: makes decisions on a consensus basis, as defined in the bylaws of the watershed group.

paragraph.heading: Watershed management project.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “watershed management project” means any project (including a demonstration project) that—

subparagraph.content: enhances water conservation, including alternative water uses;
improves water quality;
improves ecological resiliency of a river or stream, including benefits to fisheries, wildlife, or habitat;
reduces the potential for water conflicts; or
advances any other goals associated with water quality or quantity that the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after March 30, 2009, the Secretary shall establish a program, to be known as the “Cooperative Watershed Management Program” , under which the Secretary shall provide grants—

subparagraph.content: to form a watershed group; or
to enlarge a watershed group; and

paragraph.content: to conduct 1 or more projects in accordance with the goals of a watershed group.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Application Process; Criteria.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than September 30, 2021, the Secretary shall update—

paragraph.content: the application process for the program; and
in consultation with the States, the prioritization and eligibility criteria for considering applications submitted in accordance with the application process.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In distributing grant funds under this section, the Secretary—

subparagraph.content: shall comply with paragraph (2); and

subparagraph.chapeau: may give priority to watershed groups that—

clause.content: represent maximum diversity of interests; or
serve subbasin-sized watersheds with an 8-digit hydrologic unit code, as defined by the United States Geological Survey.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary may provide to a grant recipient a first-phase grant in an amount not greater than $100,000 each year for a period of not more than 3 years.

clause.heading: Mandatory use of funds.—
clause.chapeau: The Secretary may provide to a grant recipient a first-phase grant in an amount not greater than $100,000 each year for a period of not more than 3 years.

subclause.content: to establish or enlarge a watershed group;
to develop a mission statement for the watershed group;
to develop project concepts; and
to develop a restoration plan.

subclause.heading: Determination.—
subclause.content: For each year of a first-phase grant, not later than 270 days after the date on which a grant recipient first receives grant funds for the year, the Secretary shall determine whether the grant recipient has made sufficient progress during the year to justify additional funding.

subclause.heading: Effect of determination.—
subclause.content: If the Secretary determines under subclause (I) that the progress of a grant recipient during the year covered by the determination justifies additional funding, the Secretary shall provide to the grant recipient grant funds for the following year.

clause.heading: Advancement of conditions.—
clause.chapeau: A grant recipient shall not be eligible to receive a second-phase grant under subparagraph (B) until the date on which the Secretary determines that the watershed group—

subclause.content: has approved articles of incorporation and bylaws governing the organization; and

item.content: holds regular meetings;
has completed a mission statement; and
has developed a restoration plan and project concepts for the watershed.

clause.heading: Exception.—
clause.content: A watershed group that has not applied for or received first-phase grants may apply for and receive second-phase grants under subparagraph (B) if the Secretary determines that the group has satisfied the requirements of first-phase grants.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: A watershed group may apply for and receive second-phase grants of $1,000,000 each year for a period of not more than 4 years if—

subclause.content: the watershed group has applied for and received watershed grants under subparagraph (A); or
the Secretary determines that the watershed group has satisfied the requirements of first-phase grants.

clause.heading: Mandatory use of funds.—
clause.content: A grant recipient that receives a second-phase grant shall use the funds to plan and carry out watershed management projects.

subclause.heading: Determination.—
subclause.content: For each year of the second-phase grant, not later than 270 days after the date on which a grant recipient first receives grant funds for the year, the Secretary shall determine whether the grant recipient has made sufficient progress during the year to justify additional funding.

subclause.heading: Effect of determination.—
subclause.content: If the Secretary determines under subclause (I) that the progress of a grant recipient during the year justifies additional funding, the Secretary shall provide to the grant recipient grant funds for the following year.

clause.heading: Advancement condition.—
clause.chapeau: A grant recipient shall not be eligible to receive a third-phase grant under subparagraph (C) until the date on which the Secretary determines that the grant recipient has-

subclause.content: completed each requirement of the second-phase grant; and

demonstrated that 1 or more pilot projects of the grant recipient have resulted in demonstrable improvements, as determined by the Secretary, in the functioning condition of at least 1 river or stream in the watershed.

subclause.heading: In general.—
subclause.content: Except as provided in subclause (II), the Secretary may provide to a grant recipient a third-phase grant in an amount not greater than $5,000,000 for a period of not more than 5 years.

subclause.heading: Exception.—
subclause.content: The Secretary may provide to a grant recipient a third-phase grant in an amount that is greater than the amount described in subclause (I) if the Secretary determines that the grant recipient is capable of using the additional amount to further the purposes of the program in a way that could not otherwise be achieved by the grant recipient using the amount described in subclause (I).

clause.heading: Mandatory use of funds.—
clause.content: A grant recipient that receives a third-phase grant shall use the funds to plan and carry out at least 1 watershed management project.

paragraph.heading: Authorizing use of funds for administrative and other costs.—
paragraph.chapeau: A grant recipient that receives a grant under this section may use the funds—

subparagraph.chapeau: to pay for—

clause.chapeau: administrative and coordination costs, if the costs are not greater than the lesser of—

subclause.content: 20 percent of the total amount of the grant; or

clause.content: the salary of not more than 1 full-time employee of the watershed group; and
any legal fees arising from the establishment of the relevant watershed group; and

subparagraph.chapeau: to fund—

clause.content: water quality and quantity studies of the relevant watershed; and
the planning, design, and implementation of any projects relating to water quality or quantity.

paragraph.heading: Planning.—
paragraph.content: The Federal share of the cost of an activity provided assistance through a first-phase grant shall be 100 percent.

paragraph.heading: Projects carried out under second phase.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Federal share of the cost of any activity of a watershed management project provided assistance through a second-phase grant shall not exceed 50 percent of the total cost of the activity.

subparagraph.heading: Form of non-federal share.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share under subparagraph (A) may be in the form of in-kind contributions.

paragraph.heading: Projects carried out under third phase.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Federal share of the costs of any activity of a watershed group of a grant recipient relating to a watershed management project provided assistance through a third-phase grant shall not exceed 50 percent of the total costs of the watershed management project.

subparagraph.heading: Form of non-federal share.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share under subparagraph (A) may be in the form of in-kind contributions.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date on which a grant recipient first receives funds under this section, and annually thereafter, in accordance with paragraph (2), the watershed group shall submit to the Secretary a report that describes the progress of the watershed group.

paragraph.heading: Required degree of detail.—
paragraph.content: The contents of an annual report required under paragraph (1) shall contain sufficient information to enable the Secretary to complete each report required under subsection (f), as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 5 years after March 30, 2009, and every 5 years thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate and the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives a report that describes—

paragraph.chapeau: the ways in which the program assists the Secretary—

subparagraph.content: in addressing water conflicts;
in conserving water;
in improving water quality; and
in improving the ecological resiliency of a river or stream; and

paragraph.content: benefits that the program provides, including, to the maximum extent practicable, a quantitative analysis of economic, social, and environmental benefits.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section—

paragraph.content: $2,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 and 2009;
$5,000,000 for fiscal year 2010;
$10,000,000 for fiscal year 2011; and
$20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2012 through 20212.

section.heading: SNAKE, BOISE, AND PAYETTE RIVER SYSTEMS, IDAHO.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Bureau of Reclamation, may conduct feasibility studies on projects that address water shortages within the Snake, Boise, and Payette River systems in the State of Idaho, and are considered appropriate for further study by the Bureau of Reclamation Boise Payette water storage assessment report issued during 2006.

subsection.heading: Bureau of Reclamation.—
subsection.content: A study conducted under this section shall comply with Bureau of Reclamation policy standards and guidelines for studies.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary of the Interior to carry out this section $3,000,000.

subsection.heading: Termination of Effectiveness.—
subsection.content: The authority provided by this section terminates on the date that is 20 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Findings.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may provide any grant to, or enter into an agreement with, any eligible applicant to assist the eligible applicant in planning, designing, or constructing any improvement—

subparagraph.content: drought, population increases, and environmental needs are exacerbating water supply issues across the western United States, including the Rio Grande Basin in New Mexico;

a report developed by the Bureau of Reclamation and the Bureau of Indian Affairs in 2000 identified a serious need for the rehabilitation and repair of irrigation infrastructure of the Rio Grande Pueblos;

inspection of existing irrigation infrastructure of the Rio Grande Pueblos shows that many key facilities, such as diversion structures and main conveyance ditches, are unsafe and barely, if at all, operable;

subparagraph.chapeau: the benefits of rehabilitating and repairing irrigation infrastructure of the Rio Grande Pueblos include—

clause.content: to address any climate-related impact to the water supply of the United States that increases ecological resiliency to the impacts of climate change;
extending available water supplies;
increased agricultural productivity;
economic benefits;
safer facilities; and
the preservation of the culture of Indian Pueblos in the State;

subparagraph.content: certain Indian Pueblos in the Rio Grande Basin receive water from facilities operated or owned by the Bureau of Reclamation; and

subparagraph.chapeau: to prevent the decline of species that the United States Fish and Wildlife Service and National Marine Fisheries Service have proposed for listing under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.) (or candidate species that are being considered by those agencies for such listing but are not yet the subject of a proposed rule);

clause.content: overall water management by the Bureau of Reclamation; and
the ability of the Bureau of Reclamation to help address potential water supply conflicts in the Rio Grande Basin.

paragraph.heading: Purpose.—
paragraph.chapeau: The purpose of this section is to direct the Secretary—

subparagraph.content: to assess the condition of the irrigation infrastructure of the Rio Grande Pueblos;
submit to the Secretary an application that includes a proposal of the improvement or activity to be planned, designed, constructed, or implemented by the eligible applicant.
to implement projects to rehabilitate and improve the irrigation infrastructure of the Rio Grande Pueblos.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: 2004 AGREEMENT.—
paragraph.content: The term “2004 Agreement” means the agreement entitled “Agreement By and Between the United States of America and the Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District, Providing for the Payment of Operation and Maintenance Charges on Newly Reclaimed Pueblo Indian Lands in the Middle Rio Grande Valley, New Mexico” and executed in September 2004 (including any successor agreements and amendments to the agreement).

paragraph.heading: Designated engineer.—
paragraph.content: The term “designated engineer” means a Federal employee designated under the Act of February 14, 1927 (69 Stat. 1098, chapter 138) to represent the United States in any action involving the maintenance, rehabilitation, or preservation of the condition of any irrigation structure or facility on land located in the Six Middle Rio Grande Pueblos.

paragraph.heading: District.—
paragraph.content: The term “District” means the Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District, a political subdivision of the State established in 1925.

paragraph.heading: Pueblo irrigation infrastructure.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Pueblo irrigation infrastructure” means any diversion structure, conveyance facility, or drainage facility that is—

subparagraph.content: in existence as of the date of enactment of this Act; and

subparagraph.chapeau: located on land of a Rio Grande Pueblo that is associated with—

clause.content: the delivery of water for the irrigation of agricultural land; or
the delivery of water for the irrigation of agricultural land; or

paragraph.heading: Rio grande basin.—
paragraph.content: The term “Rio Grande Basin” means the headwaters of the Rio Chama and the Rio Grande Rivers (including any tributaries) from the State line between Colorado and New Mexico downstream to the elevation corresponding with the spillway crest of Elephant Butte Dam at 4,457.3 feet mean sea level.

paragraph.heading: Rio grande pueblo.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Rio Grande Pueblo” means any of the 18 Pueblos that—

subparagraph.content: occupy land in the Rio Grande Basin; and
are included on the list of federally recognized Indian tribes published by the Secretary in accordance with section 104 of the Federally Recognized Indian Tribe List Act of 1994 (25 U.S.C. 479a-1).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Commissioner of Reclamation.

paragraph.heading: Six middle rio grande pueblos.—
paragraph.content: The term “Six Middle Rio Grande Pueblos” means each of the Pueblos of Cochiti, Santo Domingo, San Felipe, Santa Ana, Sandia, and Isleta.

paragraph.heading: Special project.—
paragraph.content: The term “special project” has the meaning given the term in the 2004 Agreement.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means the State of New Mexico.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: On the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in accordance with subparagraph (B), and in consultation with the Rio Grande Pueblos, shall—

clause.content: conduct a study of Pueblo irrigation infrastructure; and

based on the results of the study, develop a list of projects (including a cost estimate for each project), that are recommended to be implemented over a 10-year period to repair, rehabilitate, or reconstruct Pueblo irrigation infrastructure.

subparagraph.heading: Required consent.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In carrying out subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall only include each individual Rio Grande Pueblo that notifies the Secretary that the Pueblo consents to participate in—

clause.content: the conduct of the study under subparagraph (A)(i); and
the development of the list of projects under subparagraph (A)(ii) with respect to the Pueblo.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: In developing the list of projects under paragraph (1)(A)(ii), the Secretary shall—

subclause.content: consider each of the factors described in subparagraph (B); and

subclause.chapeau: prioritize the projects recommended for implementation based on—

item.content: a review of each of the factors; and
a consideration of the projected benefits of the project on completion of the project.

clause.heading: Eligibility of projects.—
clause.content: A project is eligible to be considered and prioritized by the Secretary if the project addresses at least 1 factor described in subparagraph (B).

subparagraph.heading: Factors.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The factors referred to in subparagraph (A) are—

subclause.content: the extent of disrepair of the Pueblo irrigation infrastructure; and
the effect of the disrepair on the ability of the applicable Rio Grande Pueblo to irrigate agricultural land using Pueblo irrigation infrastructure;

clause.content: whether, and the extent that, the repair, rehabilitation, or reconstruction of the Pueblo irrigation infrastructure would provide an opportunity to conserve water;

subclause.content: the economic and cultural impacts that the Pueblo irrigation infrastructure that is in disrepair has on the applicable Rio Grande Pueblo; and
the economic and cultural benefits that the repair, rehabilitation, or reconstruction of the Pueblo irrigation infrastructure would have on the applicable Rio Grande Pueblo;

clause.content: the opportunity to address water supply or environmental conflicts in the applicable river basin if the Pueblo irrigation infrastructure is repaired, rehabilitated, or reconstructed; and
the overall benefits of the project to efficient water operations on the land of the applicable Rio Grande Pueblo.

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.chapeau: In developing the list of projects under paragraph (1)(A)(ii), the Secretary shall consult with the Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs (including the designated engineer with respect to each proposed project that affects the Six Middle Rio Grande Pueblos), the Chief of the Natural Resources Conservation Service, and the Chief of Engineers to evaluate the extent to which programs under the jurisdiction of the respective agencies may be used—

subparagraph.content: to assist in evaluating projects to repair, rehabilitate, or reconstruct Pueblo irrigation infrastructure; and

subparagraph.chapeau: to implement—

clause.content: a project recommended for implementation under paragraph (1)(A)(ii); or

any other related project (including on-farm improvements) that may be appropriately coordinated with the repair, rehabilitation, or reconstruction of Pueblo irrigation infrastructure to improve the efficient use of water in the Rio Grande Basin.

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate and the Committee on Resources of the House of Representatives a report that includes—

subparagraph.content: the list of projects recommended for implementation under paragraph (1)(A)(ii); and

subparagraph.chapeau: The factors referred to in subparagraph (A) are—any findings of the Secretary with respect to—

clause.content: the study conducted under paragraph (1)(A)(i);
the consideration of the factors under paragraph (2)(B); and
the consultations under paragraph (3).

paragraph.heading: Periodic review.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 4 years after the date on which the Secretary submits the report under paragraph (4) and every 4 years thereafter, the Secretary, in consultation with each Rio Grande Pueblo, shall—

subparagraph.content: review the report submitted under paragraph (4); and
update the list of projects described in paragraph (4)(A) in accordance with each factor described in paragraph (2)(B), as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may provide grants to, and enter into contracts or other agreements with, the Rio Grande Pueblos to plan, design, construct, or otherwise implement projects to repair, rehabilitate, reconstruct, or replace Pueblo irrigation infrastructure that are recommended for implementation under subsection (c)(1)(A)(ii)—

subparagraph.content: to increase water use efficiency and agricultural productivity for the benefit of a Rio Grande Pueblo;
to conserve water; or
to otherwise enhance water management or help avert water supply conflicts in the Rio Grande Basin.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.chapeau: Assistance provided under paragraph (1) shall not be used for—

subparagraph.content: the repair, rehabilitation, or reconstruction of any major impoundment structure; or
any on-farm improvements.

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out a project under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: consult with, and obtain the approval of, the applicable Rio Grande Pueblo;
consult with the Director of the Bureau of Indian Affairs; and
as appropriate, coordinate the project with any work being conducted under the irrigation operations and maintenance program of the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

subparagraph.heading: Federal share.—
subparagraph.chapeau: the list of projects recommended for implementation under paragraph (1)(A)(ii); and

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Except as provided in clause (ii), the Federal share of the total cost of carrying out a project under paragraph (1) shall be not more than 75 percent.

clause.heading: Exception.—
clause.content: The Secretary may waive or limit the non-Federal share required under clause (i) if the Secretary determines, based on a demonstration of financial hardship by the Rio Grande Pueblo, that the Rio Grande Pueblo is unable to contribute the required non-Federal share.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary may accept from the District a partial or total contribution toward the non-Federal share required for a project carried out under paragraph (1) on land located in any of the Six Middle Rio Grande Pueblos if the Secretary determines that the project is a special project.

clause.heading: Limitation.—
clause.content: Nothing in clause (i) requires the District to contribute to the non-Federal share of the cost of a project carried out under paragraph (1).

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: The Secretary may accept from the State a partial or total contribution toward the non-Federal share for a project carried out under paragraph (1).

clause.heading: Limitation.—
clause.content: Nothing in clause (i) requires the State to contribute to the non-Federal share of the cost of a project carried out under paragraph (1).

subparagraph.heading: Form of non-federal share.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share under subparagraph (A)(i) may be in the form of in-kind contributions, including the contribution of any valuable asset or service that the Secretary determines would substantially contribute to a project carried out under paragraph (1).

paragraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may not use any amount made available under subsection (g)(2) to carry out the operation or maintenance of any project carried out under paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Effect on Existing Authority and Responsibilities.—
subsection.chapeau: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section, to remain available until expended.

paragraph.content: affects any existing project-specific funding authority; or

limits or absolves the United States from any responsibility to any Rio Grande Pueblo (including any responsibility arising from a trust relationship or from any Federal law (including regulations), Executive order, or agreement between the Federal Government and any Rio Grande Pueblo).

subsection.heading: Effect on Pueblo Water Rights or State Water Law.—

paragraph.heading: Pueblo water rights.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this section (including the implementation of any project carried out in accordance with this section) affects the right of any Pueblo to receive, divert, store, or claim a right to water, including the priority of right and the quantity of water associated with the water right under Federal or State law.

paragraph.heading: State water law.—
paragraph.chapeau: Nothing in this section preempts or affects—

subparagraph.content: State water law; or
an interstate compact governing water.
